chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Abu Haneefa: 'O Abu Haneefa! What do you say regarding a house that fell upon a group of people, and two children remained from them, one of whom was free and the other a slave of his companion, and the free one was not distinguished from the slave?' So Abu Haneefa said, 'Half of this one is liberated, and half of this one is liberated, and the wealth is divided between them.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not like that, but a lot is drawn between them, so whoever the lot hits, he is free, and this one is liberated, so he is made a master to him.'

key_terms.نِصْفُ هَذَا: Half of this (referring to the person)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling when a free child and a slave child are indistinguishable after a disaster?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the jurisprudential debate between the Hanafi school and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the inheritance of status when two children, one free and one slave, are indistinguishable after a collapse. While Abu Hanifa proposed splitting the freedom of each child, the Imam established the principle of *qur'a* (lottery), where the free child is identified by lot and the other is fully emancipated, becoming his *mawla*. This ruling underscores the Shia preference for certainty in manumission and clarifies the master-client relationship in cases of ambiguous inheritance.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to Abu Haneefa: ‘O Abu Haneefa! What are you saying regard a house which fell upon a group of people, and there remained two children from them, one of the free and the other one a slave of his companion, but the free is not recognised from the slave?’ So Abu Haneefa said, ‘Half of this should be liberated, and half of this, and the wealth be distributed between the two of them’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not like that, but a lot be drawn between the two of them, so the one who is hit by the lot, so he would be free, and this one be liberated, so he is made to be a master of his’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from al- Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar who has narrated the following:

“Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to abu Hanifah, ‘O abu Hanifah, what do you say about the case of a people who all die because of the fall of a house? Only two children remain, of whom one is free and the other is a slave of his companion but it is not known which is which’ Abu Hanifah said, ‘One-half of this and one-half of this is set free and the asset must be divided between the two.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘It is not as that. By means of raffle whoever ’s name comes out is free and this one is set free to become the Mawla ’ (master) for him.’”
